Picture: Night in the candlelit Little Chamber, rain streaking the small window. The Girl sits at the spinning wheel with a hopeless tangle of pale-gold flax in her lap and looks up in surprise: the door has creaked open, and three old faces peer round it, one above the other: the Long-Nosed Aunt at the top with her enormous nose poking far into the room, the Teary-Eyed Aunt in the middle dabbing her huge eyes, and the Broad-Hipped Aunt at the bottom, her wide striped skirt filling the doorway.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Girl: A slim, cheerful hunter's daughter of about eighteen with an oval face dusted all over with freckles, a snub nose, big hazel eyes, a wide smile and mousy-brown hair in one thick plait over her shoulder. She wears a plain pine-green linen dress with the sleeves rolled up, a short brown sheepskin vest, a leather belt and sturdy brown shoes, and has a blue jay feather tucked behind one ear.
- the Long-Nosed Aunt: A small, slim, spry old woman of about eighty who holds herself very upright, with a kindly, wrinkled face, merry little blue eyes, rosy cheeks and crooked, work-worn hands. Her nose is enormous: thick as a cucumber at the root and nearly six feet long, it sticks straight out in front of her like a branch and ends in a round pink tip. Her white hair is in a small knot. She wears a long nut-brown dress and a big moss-green fringed shawl, and leans on a crooked walking stick.
- the Teary-Eyed Aunt: A round-shouldered old woman of about eighty, of middle height, with a soft, wrinkled face and enormous round eyes as big as small plates, red-rimmed and always running with tears, so she keeps dabbing them with a big white lace handkerchief. Her silver hair is braided and pinned in a ring on top of her head. She wears a dusty-rose dress with a white collar, a red tomato-shaped pincushion on her wrist and a silver thimble on one finger.
- the Broad-Hipped Aunt: A short old woman of about eighty with narrow shoulders, a small round head and enormously broad hips and backside, so wide that she can only just squeeze through a door and her skirt looks like a haystack. She has a square little face, a snub nose, bright squinting eyes, a gap-toothed grin and grey hair in a tight bun under a small round black felt hat. She wears a huge, bell-shaped skirt with wide red and ochre stripes, a white blouse and a short dark-brown knitted jacket.

Setting:
- the Little Chamber: A small room of its own up under the roof of the royal manor, with dark log walls and a low, beamed ceiling. A narrow wooden bed with a woollen blanket stands against one wall, a small table and a candlestick sit under a four-paned leaded window with rain running down the glass, a wooden spinning wheel stands beside it, a big upright wooden loom fills the far corner, and a plank door has an iron latch.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The royal manor is a big cluster of dark log buildings with turf roofs, carved gables and small leaded windows around a cobbled yard. The flax is soft, pale-gold fibre in a great heap; spun, it becomes smooth, shining pale-gold thread wound in coils; woven, it becomes a thick bolt of fine cream-white linen; sewn, it becomes a pile of white linen shirts with buttons. The Queen's other maids are three young women in grey wool dresses, white aprons and white linen caps. The wedding feast is held in the Great Hall, with a long table, candles and six guests in festive clothes.

This story's season, light and colours: A long, rainy early autumn at the royal manor: silver rain on small leaded windows, dripping gardens with the first yellow leaves and soft grey-violet skies, then fresh, rain-washed mornings with sun on wet cobbles. Indoors: warm candle and firelight on pale-gold thread, cream linen and white shirts, and a wedding feast glowing with candles and red-and-green rosemaling. Accents: flax gold and the Queen's rainbow-striped knitting.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. characters.name: Jenta
characters.description: Datteren til en fattig jeger; snill og vakker, men uten erfaring med håndarbeid, og redd for å bli avslørt ved hoffet.
characters.look: A slim, cheerful hunter's daughter of about eighteen with an oval face dusted all over with freckles, a snub nose, big hazel eyes, a wide smile and mousy-brown hair in one thick plait over her shoulder. She wears a plain pine-green linen dress with the sleeves rolled up, a short brown sheepskin vest, a leather belt and sturdy brown shoes, and has a blue jay feather tucked behind one ear.

characters.name: Bruden
characters.description: Jenta på bryllupsdagen, med brudekrone. Nå er den store dagen kommet, og hun har lovet å kalle tre gamle koner moster.
characters.look: A slim young bride of about eighteen with an oval face dusted with freckles, a snub nose, big hazel eyes and a wide smile, her mousy-brown hair brushed out long and wavy over her shoulders under a tall silver bridal crown hung with little dangling spangles. She wears a long cream wool dress embroidered with red and green flowers at the hem and cuffs, a red woven sash, and a blue jay feather tucked behind one ear.

characters.name: Dronningen
characters.description: Liker jenta godt og elsker håndarbeid, men lar seg lett påvirke av sladder og krav om prestasjoner.
characters.look: A tall, willowy, kindly queen of about fifty with a long neck, a long oval face, crinkly grey eyes, a slightly long nose and dark hair streaked with silver in a low, coiled knot under a small gold crown. She wears a sea-green wool gown with a cream linen collar and a long rainbow-striped knitted shawl, and she is never without her knitting: two long wooden needles, a half-finished striped scarf and a ball of pink yarn.

characters.name: Prinsen
characters.description: Blir glad i jenta og gifter seg med henne, men blir sjokkert når de tre «mostrene» dukker opp i bryllupet.
characters.look: A tall, slender, polite young prince of about twenty with a long, clean-shaven face, a dimpled chin, a long nose with a little bump, earnest dark eyes under thick eyebrows and short, tidy black curls. He wears a small silver circlet, a deep-teal wool tunic with a row of silver buttons, a cream linen shirt, charcoal breeches and tall tan leather boots.

characters.name: Mosteren med den lange nesa
characters.description: Den første mosteren, som spinner alt linet for jenta på én natt. Hun har sittet ved rokken og nikket og nikket hele livet, og nå er nesa nesten to meter lang.

- the Bride: A slim young bride of about eighteen with an oval face dusted with freckles, a snub nose, big hazel eyes and a wide smile, her mousy-brown hair brushed out long and wavy over her shoulders under a tall silver bridal crown hung with little dangling spangles. She wears a long cream wool dress embroidered with red and green flowers at the hem and cuffs, a red woven sash, and a blue jay feather tucked behind one ear.
- the Long-Nosed Aunt: A small, slim, spry old woman of about eighty who holds herself very upright, with a kindly, wrinkled face, merry little blue eyes, rosy cheeks and crooked, work-worn hands. Her nose is enormous: thick as a cucumber at the root and nearly six feet long, it sticks straight out in front of her like a branch and ends in a round pink tip. Her white hair is in a small knot. She wears a long nut-brown dress and a big moss-green fringed shawl, and leans on a crooked walking stick.
- the Broad-Hipped Aunt: A short old woman of about eighty with narrow shoulders, a small round head and enormously broad hips and backside, so wide that she can only just squeeze through a door and her skirt looks like a haystack. She has a square little face, a snub nose, bright squinting eyes, a gap-toothed grin and grey hair in a tight bun under a small round black felt hat. She wears a huge, bell-shaped skirt with wide red and ochre stripes, a white blouse and a short dark-brown knitted jacket.
- the Teary-Eyed Aunt: A round-shouldered old woman of about eighty, of middle height, with a soft, wrinkled face and enormous round eyes as big as small plates, red-rimmed and always running with tears, so she keeps dabbing them with a big white lace handkerchief. Her silver hair is braided and pinned in a ring on top of her head. She wears a dusty-rose dress with a white collar, a red tomato-shaped pincushion on her wrist and a silver thimble on one finger.

Setting:
- the Great Hall: A long, warm feasting hall of dark timber with a high ceiling and red-and-green rosemaling on the carved beams, lit by candles in iron chandeliers. Down the middle runs a long table covered with a white linen cloth and set with pewter dishes, tall candles and bowls of garden flowers, with benches and carved chairs along both sides. At one end stands a tall, carved double door.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The royal manor is a big cluster of dark log buildings with turf roofs, carved gables and small leaded windows around a cobbled yard. The flax is soft, pale-gold fibre in a great heap; spun, it becomes smooth, shining pale-gold thread wound in coils; woven, it becomes a thick bolt of fine cream-white linen; sewn, it becomes a pile of white linen shirts with buttons. The Queen's other maids are three young women in grey wool dresses, white aprons and white linen caps. The wedding feast is held in the Great Hall, with a long table, candles and six guests in festive clothes.

This story's season, light and colours: A long, rainy early autumn at the royal manor: silver rain on small leaded windows, dripping gardens with the first yellow leaves and soft grey-violet skies, then fresh, rain-washed mornings with sun on wet cobbles. Indoors: warm candle and firelight on pale-gold thread, cream linen and white shirts, and a wedding feast glowing with candles and red-and-green rosemaling. Accents: flax gold and the Queen's rainbow-striped knitting.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Suitable for readers of all ages: no blood, wounds or gore, and no killing shown. Show danger and cruelty through atmosphere, posture and suspense, never through injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.
